proposed_from.topic: Four-slice ATT recovery on an absorbing Markov face. Observe iid five-date panels on states {a,b,e}, e absorbing, with treatment adoption at date 3, two known latent types, type-conditional first-order Markov potential paths, no anticipation, cohort/type overlap, and common type-specific untreated transitions. On the declared face with no date-1 absorption, four nonsingular matched active-state slices, simple cycle-product spectrum, nonzero stochastic normalizations, separated common untreated cross-ratios, and buffered variance margins, prove that spectral projectors and row-sum normalization recover type masses, the component path law through date 3, and type-specific plus aggregate first-post state ATTs over the full compatible fiber. Derive guarded empirical-cell plug-in, the saturated finite-multinomial canonical gradient, and uniform Gaussian-multiplier bands. Use the exact H1,H2,Q1,Q2,V1,V2 witness with K=[[29/5,-12/5],[8/5,1/5]], type exit ATTs (-1/25,1/20), aggregate 1/200, and the initial-absorption counterexample. Distinguish Ahn–Kasahara, Markov-mixture reconstruction, Deaner–Ku, and restricted-HMM results; Rao–Risch is the interpretation consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Four matched slices yield K=B_a diag(rho_1,rho_2) B_a^-1; projector normalization B_a=[P_1m_a,P_2m_a], terminal row sums, full-row-rank pseudoinverses, and the no-initial-absorption condition then recover all promised factors. Exact enumeration reproduces state-vector ATTs (1/25,0,-1/25) and (-1/40,-1/40,1/20), aggregate (3/400,-1/80,1/200), while an outside-face construction preserves active slices but changes type effects. Differential recurrences and compact-margin Taylor bounds were derived, with numerical derivatives agreeing to relative error 3.7e-10. Checks covered scaling, equal weights, time variation, pseudoinverses, mass normalization, cohort labels, singular boundaries, support deletion, and neighboring literature; no collision or identification failure survived. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Verify Gaussian-max quantile continuity uniformly over the compact margin class, including singular correlation limits, and combine it with the buffered empirical guard; standard bounded triangular-array CLT and finite-multinomial information steps remain explicit compressions. EARLY KILL TEST: Run the draft's exact witness verifier, differentiate its recovery map on the 120-cell support face, and test positive coordinate variances plus singular-covariance max-quantile continuity; failure of rational ATT recovery or verbatim coverage by an existing theorem stops the run. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_absorbing_four_slice_att_recovery.md.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The theorem-level delta is not spectral cancellation itself. It is recovery on a support face excluded by the closest all-state rank and positivity conditions: active spectral projectors are scaled by predecessor masses, full terminal row sums restore exit probabilities, a full-row-rank pseudoinverse transports the second predecessor factor, and absence of date-1 absorption exhausts each type mass. The inference delta is uniform guard acceptance and multiplier coverage for this analytic map under singular ATT correlation. The exact witness and outside-face observational-equivalence pair certify nonvacuity and the boundary of conditional type-effect recovery.

seed_details.title: Absorbing-face full-fiber recovery
seed_details.anchor_location: Proposition 14, Assumption ID(a)--(b), and Appendix A.4 equations (33)--(37); Introduction contributions 1--3 and final empirical application section were read.
seed_details.opportunity: Replace the anchor's invertible all-state terminal factors by four active minors, projector normalization, full terminal row sums, and a support-face mass equation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After the four-slice cancellation, normalize projector columns with \(m_a\) and use all three terminal columns before transporting \(B_b\) with a full-row-rank pseudoinverse.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Ahn--Kasahara after deleting the absorbing state.
seed_details.rebuttal: Deletion produces substochastic active rows, while conditioning on future survival changes type weights and cohort transitions; the row-sum and no-initial-absorption normalization is a new proof step.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The kernel is a computable recovery theorem over the full compatible fiber, not identification by an opaque functional or a single witness.

seed_details.title: Guarded singular-correlation multiplier bands
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 4 equations (20)--(25) and Appendix C weighted bootstrap and uniform confidence intervals; Introduction and final applications were read.
seed_details.opportunity: Prove uniform acceptance, linearization, covariance consistency, and simultaneous coverage for a rational spectral plug-in on a structural-zero face.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Establish a common analytic neighborhood from buffered inverse and normalization margins before applying Gaussian comparison at singular correlation limits.
seed_details.red_team: A finite-dimensional delta method plus Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato makes this automatic.
seed_details.rebuttal: The data-dependent guard, uniform Taylor neighborhood, label stability, and positive-diagonal but singular covariance must be integrated; none is delivered by the anchor's pointwise interior MLE argument.
seed_details.decision: survives and folded into selected package
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is an explicit limit-law and coverage result for a named estimator, not a bare inference add-on.

seed_details.title: Constrained Markov efficiency bound
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 4 likelihood estimator and Appendix C; the paper's identification proof and motivation were also read.
seed_details.opportunity: Project the saturated recovery gradient onto the tangent space generated by common kernels, latent Markov factorization, and fifth-date restrictions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the polynomial image defining the compatible Markov law and characterize the closure of its score range before projecting \(G_p\).
seed_details.red_team: Finite-dimensional parametric likelihood efficiency is routine once the model is identified.
seed_details.rebuttal: Structural zeros, latent-label quotienting, and redundant polynomial restrictions make the tangent rank law-dependent; the presolve establishes only saturated-model efficiency.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The efficiency bound and attaining estimator are the named focal objects; no oracle nuisance assumption supplies them.

seed_details.title: Sharp ATT bounds with initial absorbers
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction discussion of absorbing binary outcomes and Section 2.1 identification under common dynamics and proportional hazards; conclusion and application discussion were read.
seed_details.opportunity: Optimize each ATT coordinate over every stochastic two-type Markov factorization reproducing the five-date law when baseline exit can be allocated across types.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the linear hazard recursion by a polynomial compatible-fiber program and certify endpoint attainment by valid component laws.
seed_details.red_team: Duarte et al.'s generic polynomial program already gives the bounds.
seed_details.rebuttal: A generic solver gives certified numerical extrema, not the requested analytic endpoints, collapse conditions, or bound-specific inference for this nonlinear Markov fiber.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The intended deliverable is endpoint-attaining sharp bounds and an inference rung, not an unspecified infimum over latent laws.

seed_details.title: Joint weak-margin localization frontier
seed_details.anchor_location: Main theorem program for weak, semi-strong, and strong drifting sequences, stochastic quadratic expansions, and identification-robust confidence sets; Introduction and applications were read.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive rates and limit experiments as the eigengap, slice singular values, and row-sum normalizers shrink jointly.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Expand the nonlinear matched-slice equations under three separate shrinking margins rather than a scalar extremum-identification index.
seed_details.red_team: Andrews--Cheng already covers any extremum estimator with weak identification.
seed_details.rebuttal: Its generic theory does not supply the local experiment, attainable rate, or distinction between aggregate and labeled type effects for this multi-margin spectral map.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposal would need both attainable regimes and localization lower behavior, not merely assume an eigengap sequence.

seed_details.title: Transition-factorization sensitivity region
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction and related-literature discussion of anticipation and differential transition dynamics, together with the exact identification equations in Appendix A.4.
seed_details.opportunity: Index observable violations of common transition factorization by a radius and derive sharp ATT regions and the first sign-reversal radius.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Perturb the simultaneous factorization equations and prove global endpoint attainment rather than apply a linear mean-trend bias formula.
seed_details.red_team: This is Rambachan--Roth with transition probabilities substituted for trends.
seed_details.rebuttal: The latent stochastic factorization is nonlinear and its perturbation can amplify through eigengaps and normalizers, so neither endpoints nor the critical radius follow from linear trend sensitivity.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A credible version must produce explicit endpoints and a named critical radius; qualitative robustness would be rejected.

seed_details.title: Uniform ATT inference across the type-count boundary
seed_details.anchor_location: Main modified EM test theorem, reparameterization near homogeneity, and simulated nonstandard null maximum; Introduction and concluding discussion were read.
seed_details.opportunity: Test one versus two absorbing Markov types and invert the test for aggregate ATT confidence sets with oracle width away from the boundary.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Derive the first informative likelihood expansion for multinomial path probabilities under common absorbing zeros.
seed_details.red_team: Kasahara--Shimotsu's modified EM test transfers directly to multinomial panels.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their normal-mixture score expansion does not transfer across structural-zero constraints or propagate component selection into uniform causal-ATT coverage.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A selection-consistent estimator alone is insufficient; the kernel requires uniform confidence sets and a separation scale.

seed_details.title: Unlabeled ATT law at spectral collision
seed_details.anchor_location: Assumption ID(a)(ii) distinct eigenvalues and Appendix A.4 eigenvector recovery; Introduction motivation for latent-type effects and final applications were read.
seed_details.opportunity: Identify or refute identification of the mixing measure \(\sum_j\pi_j^1\delta_{\tau_j}\) at repeated cycle-product eigenvalues.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct basis-invariant moments of the ATT measure from matched slices without individual spectral projectors.
seed_details.red_team: Discarding labels automatically resolves spectral collision.
seed_details.rebuttal: ATT vectors compose projectors with row sums, pseudoinverses, and cohort-specific transitions, so invariance of the quotient law is not automatic and may fail observationally.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The target is the unlabeled mixing law with an identification or impossibility frontier, not arbitrarily relabeled type coefficients.

seed_details.title: Fifth-date overidentification test
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 3 latent Markov likelihood, Proposition 14, and the pre-treatment transition-independence diagnostics; Introduction and empirical applications were read.
seed_details.opportunity: Use date \(4\), which point recovery does not need, to test the common-kernel and latent Markov restrictions while retaining valid ATT inference after local misspecification.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Project unused fifth-date cell residuals off the derivative span of the four-slice recovery equations and derive their boundary-aware quadratic form.
seed_details.red_team: This is an ordinary likelihood-ratio specification test in a finite multinomial model.
seed_details.rebuttal: The absorbing face and latent labels produce rank-dependent tangent cones, though the resulting contribution is narrower than the recovery theorem.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The date-‑\(4\) residual and its tangent-space projection are named focal objects; a generic goodness-of-fit test would not suffice.
